clue.text: Former husband, first person with part in show

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
the first person singular pronoun is I
a part of something is a bit

explanation.surface: A woman's ex-husband has landed a role in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to put it on display, which is to show it.

clue.text: Infuriate a Green after recycling

indicators.note: something recycled is broken down and made into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmentalist is driven mad after the recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage is to make someone furious, the same as to infuriate.

clue.text: Focus on state's excessive pride

parts.note: a hub is the focus or centre of activity
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Concentrating on one's own state shows overweening pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state's' is RI'S: RI for Rhode Island plus the possessive S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overbearing arrogance, the pride that comes before a fall in Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Capital sort of roll with nowt taken out

parts.note: a bridge roll is a small, soft, finger-shaped bread roll

indicators.note: taken out suggests the letters are shaken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; nowt is northern English for nothing

explanation.surface: A capital bread roll with nothing removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' rearranges NOWT into TOWN. A bridge roll is a British finger roll; nowt is northern dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgetown is the capital city of Barbados.

clue.text: Not allowed cheers? I don't like that!

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thank-yous
boo is an exclamation of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone forbids drinking toasts and voices dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, as is 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, so it is not allowed.

clue.text: Hint about leading lady's patio

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a trace is a slight hint or suggestion
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: A gossip drops hints about the star actress's patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the queen inside the hint word; 'leading lady' is the crossword convention for the Queen, not an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a paved outdoor area beside a house, much the same thing as a patio.

clue.text: God with North British dicky bird

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart, so ill

explanation.surface: A god appears with a North British little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky bird' suggests a child's word for a bird, but 'dicky' means poorly, ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A thornbill is a small Australian songbird.

clue.text: Fish that's red apart from the tail

indicators.note: everything but the tail means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ruddy means red, especially of complexion

explanation.surface: A fish is red except at its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family, with red fins.

clue.text: Irish fool heartlessly following a family member? That's my opinion

indicators.note: the fool's piece comes after the other pieces

parts.note: sis is short for sister

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: eejit is Irish slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: An Irish idiot cruelly pursues a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle J from EEJIT, Irish slang for an idiot, leaving EEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: As I see it is a set phrase introducing one's own opinion.

clue.text: Close of day without time for sport

indicators.note: without is taken in its old sense of outside, so the evening encloses the time

parts.note: evening is the close of the day

explanation.surface: At the end of the day there is no time for games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but means outside here: T goes inside EVENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is an equestrian sport combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Timid person taking time off to see teacher

indicators.note: with 'off' around 'time', taking something off means removing it from the word
the second half of 'taking ... off', signalling a letter removed

parts.note: a rabbit is a timid or feeble person, often a poor sports player

explanation.surface: A shy person takes time off work to visit a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... off' removes the T from RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher, the word itself meaning 'my master'.

clue.text: More than one shot in shoulder after commencement of battle

indicators.note: the shoulder piece is placed after the opening letter
the commencement of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the hard shoulder is the strip at the side of the road, the roadside

explanation.surface: A soldier is shot in the shoulder just after the battle begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot in shoulder' reads as a wound, but 'More than one shot' is the definition, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a simultaneous firing of all the guns on one side of a ship, many shots at once.

clue.text: Revolutionary providing enough for everybody

definitions.meaning: something revolutionary is literally turning in a circle, spinning on an axis
there is enough of something to share out among all present

explanation.definitionFit: Going round means rotating, and also being sufficient for everyone to get a share.

clue.text: Put away by book club

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A book club tidies its volumes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link meaning next to; 'club' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To club someone is to hit them with a stick, which is to beat them.

clue.text: Hoarded as peanuts may be on holiday?

definitions.meaning: stored up secretly for future use

definitions.text: as peanuts may be on holiday?
definitions.meaning: peanuts are often salted, and someone on holiday is away

explanation.definitionFit: Salted away means put by for the future, and playfully describes salted nuts that are away.

clue.text: 21 people without one getting close

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the other pieces surround the numeral

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is a handle or label, and a term is likewise a name for something
a nation is a people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A list of names lacks one person as the deadline draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' refers to the answer at 21 across, here replaced by a synonym; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A termination is an end, the close of something.

clue.text: Secure telephone receiver

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A secure telephone receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' looks like the phone handset, but it is a FENCE, a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to protect it by guaranteeing it is used only for one purpose.

clue.text: Superficial variety in Bath and Wells, say, and first of all in Portishead

indicators.note: the variety goes in the diocese word

parts.note: Bath and Wells is a diocese, a bishop's see
a kind is a sort or variety

indicators.note: the first of all the letters in the word means its opening letter

explanation.surface: Various places in Somerset, Bath, Wells and Portishead, look only superficially alike.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, Wells and Portishead are all Somerset towns, but 'Bath and Wells' is a diocese; 'in' places the variety inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep describes something superficial, going no deeper than the surface.

clue.text: Sudden flight impressed European

parts.note: stamped means impressed, as a mark pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: A European was struck by a sudden flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of animals or people fleeing.

clue.text: Original sweet-talkin' actress

indicators.note: an original version can be read as one made anew from these letters, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A charming, smooth-talking actress is one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven letters of SWEETTALKIN are rearranged; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Winslet is an English film star, known for Titanic and The Reader.

clue.text: Missing suspect's first to stop a grass

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: bent is a type of grass

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A suspect is the first to stop a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' suggests an informer, but here it is BENT, a type of grass; 'to stop' puts S inside A BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, so missing.

clue.text: Songwriter once divided city

definitions.meaning: the German capital was split by a wall from 1961 to 1989

explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was a great American songwriter, and the city was split East and West in the Cold War.

clue.text: Handle sodium, more or less

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

indicators.note: less tells us the word just before it is removed from the word more

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist describes how to treat roughly that much sodium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more or less' looks like a vague qualifier, but it is MORE with OR taken away, leaving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or nickname, as in a CB radio handle.

clue.text: A story about president not breaking the bank

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so the story encloses the president

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story
Gerald Ford was the 38th US president

explanation.surface: A tale about a president who does not overspend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the president inside the story, after the initial A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affordable is cheap enough to buy without financial ruin.

clue.text: Beginning film here?

definitions.meaning: on a film set is where a movie is shot

explanation.definitionFit: Onset means a beginning, and read as two words it is where filming takes place.

clue.text: Bird not taking off in summer heat

indicators.note: in shows the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird stays grounded in the summer heat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, so it does not take off.

clue.text: Trumpeters appearing in county after Brazilian player's brought back

indicators.note: the county is placed after the turned name
brought back means the name is turned to read from end to start

parts.note: Pelé is the famous Brazilian footballer
Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A band of trumpeters appears in an English county after a Brazilian footballer returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns PELE into ELEP. HANTS is short for Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants trumpet with their trunks, so they are fancifully called trumpeters.

clue.text: We'll hear revolver

indicators.note: hear tells us the clue word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the contraction we'll is said very like the word for a turning disc

explanation.surface: A promise that we will listen to the gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' wants to be a gun; it is something that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns round on its axle, so it is literally something that revolves.

clue.text: Pastoral leader, say

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to relate a story is to say or tell it

explanation.surface: A church leader is mentioned as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a bishop leads a flock, pastorally, while the wordplay is P plus RELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop, who leads his flock as a pastor.

clue.text: Hornblower holds back in convoy to attempt something audacious

indicators.note: holds means the first piece contains the next

parts.note: Triton, the Greek sea god, blows a conch shell like a horn

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Captain Hornblower holds back in the convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hornblower suggests C S Forester's naval hero, but here it is the conch-blowing sea god Triton; 'holds' puts the Y at the back of 'convoy' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is an idiom for chancing one's luck with something cheeky or audacious.
